raw_response:
I only have 5 mu, and some people in my family work outside, so I cannot farm in a big way. I mostly follow what worked the last two years and what neighbors around me do. For wheat, I do not dare save too much on fertilizer, because if wheat turns weak in spring, yield drops fast. But I also cannot spend too much at once, so I split it: some as base fertilizer, some later when I see the crop. For maize after wheat, the time is tight, so I keep it simple, clear the wheat, do quick rotary tillage, and sow fast with hybrid seed like most people here. We have well water, so if it stays dry I will irrigate, but I will not overdo it because pumping costs money.

I am not trying anything fancy this year. I want stable grain first. If the weather is normal, wheat should do fairly well, and maize should follow if I plant on time right after harvest. I would rather use round, familiar amounts and keep a little cash in hand than spend everything chasing a higher yield.
